** Major** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Check whether another version still serves the kind before skipping deletion.** If a manifest specifies `batch/v1beta1` `CronJob`, that version can return 404 while the object still exists through `batch/v1`. Kubernetes explicitly preserves existing CronJobs across this version removal. ([kubernetes.io](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/)) This lookup then makes `kindUnserved` return true. `Delete` reports `not-found` without deleting the CronJob. Previously, the resolution error stopped deletion. Check the other served versions of the same `GroupKind`. If another version serves the kind, or discovery is inconclusive, preserve the original error. Continue to skip kinds that discovery confirms are absent.

A manifest can use a lowercase kind such as `gadget`, and the loader accepts it. If another served version lists the same kind as `Gadget`, this comparison misses it. `kindUnserved` then returns `true`, and `Delete` reports `not-found` and skips an object the cluster still serves. The original no-match error was the correct result for this case. Use a case-insensitive comparison on this line:

The client-go converter removes stale versions from `APIGroup.Versions`. `ServerGroups()` also discards the failed-version map. `kindUnserved` therefore checks only the versions that discovery returned as served.
